title: Connection API
text:
The Connection API provides asynchronous context managers for simplified NATS connection and JetStream resource management. These context managers handle the complete lifecycle of connections, including establishment, error handling, and proper cleanup.


Asynchronous context manager for establishing and managing NATS connections.
Parameters: - config (Optional[GlobalServiceConfig]): Optional configuration object for the NATS connection. If None, the default global configuration will be used.
Yields: - NATSClient: An established NATS client connection.
Raises: - NaqConnectionError: If connection establishment fails. - ErrNoServers: If no NATS servers are available. - ErrTimeout: If connection times out. - ErrConnectionClosed: If connection is closed unexpectedly.
Example:
from naq.connection import nats_connection

# Using default configuration
async with nats_connection() as nc:
    await nc.publish("subject", b"message")

# Using custom configuration
from naq.services.config import GlobalServiceConfig
config = GlobalServiceConfig(nats_url="nats://custom:4222")
async with nats_connection(config) as nc:
    await nc.publish("subject", b"message")



Asynchronous context manager for obtaining a JetStream context from a NATS connection.
Parameters: - nc (NATSClient): An established NATS client connection.
Yields: - JetStreamContext: The JetStream context for interacting with JetStream.
Raises: - NaqConnectionError: If JetStream context creation fails.
Example:
from naq.connection import nats_connection, jetstream_context

# Using with an existing NATS connection
async with nats_connection() as nc:
    async with jetstream_context(nc) as js:
        await js.add_stream(name="mystream", subjects=["my.subject"])
        await js.publish("my.subject", b"message")



Asynchronous context manager that combines NATS connection and JetStream context in a single operation.
Parameters: - config (Optional[GlobalServiceConfig]): Optional configuration object for the NATS connection. If None, the default global configuration will be used.
Yields: - A tuple containing (NATSClient, JetStreamContext) - the established NATS connection and JetStream context.
Raises: - NaqConnectionError: If connection establishment or JetStream context creation fails. - ErrNoServers: If no NATS servers are available. - ErrTimeout: If connection times out. - ErrConnectionClosed: If connection is closed unexpectedly.
Example:
from naq.connection import nats_jetstream

# Using default configuration
async with nats_jetstream() as (nc, js):
    await js.add_stream(name="mystream", subjects=["my.subject"])
    await js.publish("my.subject", b"message")

# Using custom configuration
from naq.services.config import GlobalServiceConfig
config = GlobalServiceConfig(nats_url="nats://custom:4222")
async with nats_jetstream(config) as (nc, js):
    await js.add_stream(name="mystream", subjects=["my.subject"])
    await js.publish("my.subject", b"message")



Asynchronous context manager for NATS Key-Value store operations.
Parameters: - bucket_name (str): Name of the KV bucket to access or create. - config (Optional[GlobalServiceConfig]): Optional configuration object for the NATS connection. If None, the default global configuration will be used.
Yields: - KeyValue: An established Key-Value store instance for the specified bucket.
Raises: - NaqConnectionError: If connection establishment, JetStream context creation, or KV store access fails. - ErrNoServers: If no NATS servers are available. - ErrTimeout: If connection times out. - ErrConnectionClosed: If connection is closed unexpectedly. - BucketNotFoundError: If the KV bucket doesn’t exist and auto-creation fails.
Example:
from naq.connection import nats_kv_store

# Using default configuration
async with nats_kv_store("my_bucket") as kv:
    await kv.put("key", b"value")
    value = await kv.get("key")

# Using custom configuration
from naq.services.config import GlobalServiceConfig
config = GlobalServiceConfig(nats_url="nats://custom:4222")
async with nats_kv_store("my_bucket", config) as kv:
    await kv.put("key", b"value")
    value = await kv.get("key")

from naq.connection import nats_connection

# Simple connection usage
async with nats_connection() as nc:

from naq.connection import nats_jetstream

# JetStream stream and consumer management
async with nats_jetstream() as (nc, js):
    # Create a stream
    await js.add_stream(name="events", subjects=["events.>"])
    
    # Publish messages
    await js.publish("events.user.created", b"User data")
    
    # Create a consumer
    await js.add_consumer("events", durable_name="event_processor")
    
    # Process messages
    consumer = await js.consumer("events", "event_processor")
    async for msg in consumer.messages:
        print(f"Received: {msg.subject} - {msg.data}")
        await msg.ack()



from naq.connection import nats_kv_store

# KV store for configuration or state management
async with nats_kv_store("app_config") as kv:
    # Store configuration
    await kv.put("max_workers", b"10")
    await kv.put("timeout", b"30")
    
    # Retrieve configuration
    max_workers = await kv.get("max_workers")
    timeout = await kv.get("timeout")
    print(f"Config: max_workers={max_workers.value}, timeout={timeout.value}")



from naq.connection import nats_connection, jetstream_context, nats_kv_store

# Complex workflow using multiple context managers
async with nats_connection() as nc:
    # Use JetStream for messaging
    async with jetstream_context(nc) as js:
        await js.add_stream(name="tasks", subjects=["tasks.>"])
        await js.publish("tasks.process", b"Task data")
    
    # Use KV store for state
    async with nats_kv_store("task_state") as kv:
        await kv.put("last_task", b"process")
        last_task = await kv.get("last_task")

title: Connection API
text:
The Connection API has been enhanced with the new service layer architecture to provide better integration with the ServiceManager and improved connection pooling capabilities.


For applications using the new service layer architecture, it’s recommended to use the ServiceManager for connection management:
from naq.services.manager import ServiceManager
from naq.services.base import ServiceConfig
from naq.services.connection import ConnectionServiceConfig

# Create service configuration
connection_config = ConnectionServiceConfig(
    servers=["nats://localhost:4222"],
    pool_size=10,
    connection_timeout=5.0
)

# Create service manager
service_manager = ServiceManager(config=ServiceConfig(custom_settings=connection_config.as_dict()))

# Initialize all services
await service_manager.initialize_all()

# Get connection service
connection_service = service_manager.get_service("connection", ConnectionService)

# Use the connection service
nc = await connection_service.get_connection()
await nc.publish("my.subject", b"Hello, World!")

# Clean up all services
await service_manager.cleanup_all()



The ConnectionService provides several performance optimizations:
from naq.services.connection import ConnectionService, ConnectionServiceConfig

# Configure connection service with performance optimizations
config = ConnectionServiceConfig(
    servers=["nats://localhost:4222"],
    pool_size=20,  # Larger pool for high-throughput applications
    connection_timeout=2.0,
    max_reconnect_attempts=5,
    enable_connection_pooling=True,
    enable_connection_caching=True,
    idle_connection_cleanup_interval=60.0  # Clean up idle connections every minute
)

connection_service = ConnectionService(config=config)

# Get connection statistics
stats = await connection_service.get_connection_statistics()
print(f"Active connections: {stats.active_connections}")
print(f"Connection pool size: {stats.pool_size}")
print(f"Average connection time: {stats.average_connection_time}")

title: API Reference
text:
This section provides a detailed reference for the public API of the naq library.
The API is organized into modules, each providing specific functionality.

title: API Reference
text:
Core Modules

queue Module: The primary interface for enqueuing and scheduling jobs. Includes the Queue class and helper functions like enqueue, enqueue_at, and schedule.
job Module: Defines the Job class, which represents a unit of work to be executed.
worker Module: Contains the Worker class, responsible for executing jobs from one or more queues.
scheduler Module: Contains the Scheduler class, responsible for enqueuing scheduled and recurring jobs.
connection Module: Provides utilities for managing NATS connections, including connection monitoring, metrics tracking, and connection pooling.
exceptions Module: Defines custom exceptions raised by naq.
utils Module: Provides utility functions and classes for common functionality used throughout the NAQ codebase, including validation, error handling, serialization, and more.

title: API Reference
text:
Services

services Module: Provides a comprehensive service layer with modular components for connection management, job processing, event logging, and more. Includes the ServiceManager for dependency injection, service lifecycle management, and performance monitoring.
kv_stores Module: Provides a robust, centralized service for managing NATS KeyValue stores with support for pooling, transactions, and TTL.

title: API Reference
text:
Service Layer Architecture
The service layer is the foundation of NAQ’s modular architecture, providing a clean separation of concerns and enabling flexible composition of functionality. Each service is designed to be:

Modular: Can be used independently or composed with other services
Configurable: Supports both centralized and service-specific configuration
Monitorable: Built-in performance tracking and health monitoring
Extensible: Easy to extend with custom functionality


Core Services








Service
Description
Key Features




ConnectionService
Manages NATS connections and JetStream contexts
Connection pooling, caching, automatic reconnection


ConfigService
Provides centralized configuration management
Environment variables, hierarchical settings, validation


JobService
Handles job execution and lifecycle management
Result storage, event logging, retry handling


KVStoreService
Manages NATS KeyValue stores
Transactions, TTL, history tracking


EventService
Logs and retrieves system events
Configurable retention, event types, filtering


StreamService
Manages JetStream streams
Stream creation, consumer management, message publishing


WorkerService
Tracks worker status and job processing
Heartbeat monitoring, job registration, lifecycle management


SchedulerService
Handles job scheduling and triggering
Cron expressions, one-time schedules, recurring jobs





ServiceManager
The ServiceManager is the central component that orchestrates all services:
from naq.services.base import ServiceManager

async def main():
    # Create and initialize service manager
    manager = ServiceManager()
    await manager.initialize_all()
    
    # Access services as needed
    connection_service = manager.get_service(ConnectionService)
    job_service = manager.get_service(JobService)
    
    # Use services...
    
    # Cleanup all services
    await manager.cleanup_all()


Service Configuration
Services can be configured through the centralized configuration system:
from naq.services.base import ServiceConfig
from naq.services.connection import ConnectionServiceConfig

# Create service-specific configuration
connection_config = ConnectionServiceConfig(
    servers=["nats://localhost:4222"],
    max_reconnect_attempts=10
)

# Apply to service
service_config = ServiceConfig(custom_settings=connection_config.as_dict())
connection_service = ConnectionService(config=service_config)


Migration Guide
For detailed information on migrating to the service layer, see the Migration Validation section in the architecture documentation.
For advanced usage patterns and performance optimization, see the Service Layer Architecture section in the advanced documentation.

The Job class represents a unit of work that is enqueued and executed by a worker. You typically don’t create Job instances directly; they are created for you when you call functions like naq.enqueue().
A Job instance is returned every time you enqueue a task, and it serves as a handle to that task.

text:
Service Layer Integration
The Job class integrates with the new service layer architecture to provide enhanced functionality:

Job Processing with Services
When using the ServiceManager, job processing is handled by the JobService, which provides:

Automatic event logging for job lifecycle events
Enhanced error handling and retry logic
Performance monitoring and statistics

from naq.services.manager import ServiceManager
from naq.services.base import ServiceConfig

service_manager = ServiceManager(config=ServiceConfig())
await service_manager.initialize_all()

title: KeyValue Store API
text:
Usage Examples

Basic Operations
import asyncio
from naq.services.kv_stores import KVStoreService, KVStoreServiceConfig

async def main():
    # Create a KV store service
    config = KVStoreServiceConfig(
        nats_url="nats://localhost:4222",
        pool_size=5
    )
    kv_service = KVStoreService(config)
    
    # Store a value
    await kv_service.put("my_bucket", "user:123", {"name": "Alice", "age": 30})
    
    # Retrieve a value
    user = await kv_service.get("my_bucket", "user:123")
    print(user)  # {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}
    
    # Delete a key
    deleted = await kv_service.delete("my_bucket", "user:123")
    print(f"Deleted: {deleted}")  # Deleted: True

asyncio.run(main())


Using Transactions
import asyncio
from naq.services.kv_stores import KVStoreService, KVStoreServiceConfig

async def main():
    config = KVStoreServiceConfig()
    kv_service = KVStoreService(config)
    
    try:
        async with kv_service.kv_transaction("inventory") as tx:
            # Check stock
            stock = await tx.get("item:widget", 0)
            if stock < 10:
                # Restock
                await tx.put("item:widget", stock + 50)
                # Log the restock
                await tx.put("log:restock", {"item": "widget", "amount": 50})
            # Transaction commits automatically on exit
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Transaction failed: {e}")
        # Transaction rolls back automatically on exception

asyncio.run(main())


Working with Multiple Buckets
import asyncio
from naq.services.kv_stores import KVStoreService, KVStoreServiceConfig

async def main():
    config = KVStoreServiceConfig()
    kv_service = KVStoreService(config)
    
    # Store data in different buckets
    await kv_service.put("users", "user:123", {"name": "Alice"})
    await kv_service.put("sessions", "session:abc", {"user_id": "123", "expires": "2023-12-31"})
    await kv_service.put("cache", "page:home", "<html>...</html>")
    
    # List keys in a bucket
    user_keys = await kv_service.keys("users")
    print(f"User keys: {user_keys}")

asyncio.run(main())


Error Handling
import asyncio
from naq.services.kv_stores import KVStoreService, KVStoreServiceConfig
from naq.exceptions import NaqException

async def main():
    config = KVStoreServiceConfig()
    kv_service = KVStoreService(config)
    
    try:
        # This will raise an exception for invalid bucket names
        await kv_service.put("", "key", "value")
    except NaqException as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}")
    
    try:
        # This will raise an exception for invalid keys
        await kv_service.put("bucket", "key with spaces", "value")
    except NaqException as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}")

asyncio.run(main())

title: KeyValue Store API
text:
Context Manager for KV Stores
The naq.connection module provides a convenient context manager nats_kv_store for simplified KeyValue store operations. This context manager handles the complete lifecycle of NATS connection, JetStream context, and KV store access with proper error handling and resource cleanup.

nats_kv_store(bucket_name: str, config: Optional[GlobalServiceConfig] = None)
Asynchronous context manager for NATS Key-Value store operations.
Parameters: - bucket_name (str): Name of the KV bucket to access or create. - config (Optional[GlobalServiceConfig]): Optional configuration object for the NATS connection. If None, the default global configuration will be used.
Yields: - KeyValue: An established Key-Value store instance for the specified bucket.
Raises: - NaqConnectionError: If connection establishment, JetStream context creation, or KV store access fails. - ErrNoServers: If no NATS servers are available. - ErrTimeout: If connection times out. - ErrConnectionClosed: If connection is closed unexpectedly. - BucketNotFoundError: If the KV bucket doesn’t exist and auto-creation fails.


Usage Examples


Basic KV Store Operations
import asyncio
from naq.connection import nats_kv_store

async def main():
    # Using default configuration
    async with nats_kv_store("my_bucket") as kv:
        # Store a value
        await kv.put("key", b"value")
        
        # Retrieve a value
        value = await kv.get("key")
        print(f"Retrieved: {value.value}")
        
        # Delete a key
        await kv.delete("key")
        
        # List all keys
        keys = await kv.keys()
        print(f"Keys in bucket: {keys}")

asyncio.run(main())


Working with Custom Configuration
import asyncio
from naq.connection import nats_kv_store
from naq.services.config import GlobalServiceConfig

async def main():
    # Using custom configuration
    config = GlobalServiceConfig(nats_url="nats://custom:4222")
    async with nats_kv_store("app_config", config) as kv:
        # Store configuration
        await kv.put("max_workers", b"10")
        await kv.put("timeout", b"30")
        
        # Retrieve configuration
        max_workers = await kv.get("max_workers")
        timeout = await kv.get("timeout")
        print(f"Config: max_workers={max_workers.value}, timeout={timeout.value}")

asyncio.run(main())


Complex Data with Serialization
import asyncio
import json
from naq.connection import nats_kv_store

async def main():
    async with nats_kv_store("user_data") as kv:
        # Store complex data as JSON
        user_data = {"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "preferences": {"theme": "dark"}}
        await kv.put("user:123", json.dumps(user_data).encode())
        
        # Retrieve and parse complex data
        stored_data = await kv.get("user:123")
        if stored_data:
            user = json.loads(stored_data.value.decode())
            print(f"User: {user['name']}, Age: {user['age']}")
            print(f"Theme: {user['preferences']['theme']}")

asyncio.run(main())


Error Handling
import asyncio
from naq.connection import nats_kv_store
from naq.exceptions import NaqConnectionError

async def main():
    try:
        # This will handle connection errors and bucket creation errors
        async with nats_kv_store("test_bucket") as kv:
            await kv.put("key", b"value")
            value = await kv.get("key")
            print(f"Value: {value.value}")
    except NaqConnectionError as e:
        print(f"Connection error: {e}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Unexpected error: {e}")

asyncio.run(main())


Comparison with KVStoreService
The nats_kv_store context manager provides a simpler, more direct approach to KV store operations compared to the KVStoreService:
Use nats_kv_store when: - You need simple, direct KV store operations - You want automatic connection and resource management - You’re working with a single bucket at a time - You prefer a context manager approach
Use KVStoreService when: - You need connection pooling for high-throughput applications - You require transaction support - You’re working with multiple buckets simultaneously - You need advanced features like TTL or custom serialization
# Using nats_kv_store (simple, direct)
async with nats_kv_store("config") as kv:
    await kv.put("setting", b"value")

# Using KVStoreService (advanced, pooled)
from naq.services.kv_stores import KVStoreService, KVStoreServiceConfig

config = KVStoreServiceConfig(pool_size=10)
service = KVStoreService(config)
await service.put("config", "setting", "value")
## Service Layer Integration with KVStoreService

The KVStoreService has been enhanced as part of the service layer architecture to provide better integration with the ServiceManager and improved performance.

### Using KVStoreService with ServiceManager

For applications using the service layer architecture, it's recommended to use the ServiceManager for KV store operations:

```python
from naq.services.manager import ServiceManager
from naq.services.base import ServiceConfig
from naq.services.kv_stores import KVStoreServiceConfig

# Create service configuration
kv_config = KVStoreServiceConfig(
    bucket_name="app_data",
    pool_size=10,
    enable_transactions=True
)

# Create service manager
service_manager = ServiceManager(config=ServiceConfig(custom_settings=kv_config.as_dict()))
await service_manager.initialize_all()

# Get KV store service
kv_service = service_manager.get_service("kv_stores", KVStoreService)

# Use the service
await kv_service.put("config", "setting", "value")
value = await kv_service.get("config", "setting")
print(f"Retrieved value: {value}")

# Use transactions
async with kv_service.kv_transaction("inventory") as tx:
    stock = await tx.get("item:widget", 0)
    await tx.put("item:widget", stock + 10)

# Clean up
await service_manager.cleanup_all()


Performance Considerations
The KVStoreService provides several performance optimizations:
from naq.services.kv_stores import KVStoreServiceConfig

# Configure for performance
config = KVStoreServiceConfig(
    bucket_name="high_performance_store",
    pool_size=20,  # Larger pool for high-throughput applications
    connection_timeout=2.0,
    max_retries=3,
    enable_connection_caching=True,
    enable_transactions=True
)

# Monitor performance
kv_service = KVStoreService(config)

title: Scheduler API
text:
naq.scheduler.Scheduler
You typically run the scheduler from the command line using naq scheduler, but you can also create and run a Scheduler instance programmatically.

naq.scheduler.Scheduler(nats_url, poll_interval, instance_id, enable_ha)








Parameter
Type
Description




nats_url
str
The URL of the NATS server.


poll_interval
float
The interval (in seconds) at which the scheduler checks for due jobs. Defaults to 1.0.


instance_id
str | None
A unique ID for the scheduler instance, used for High Availability. A unique ID is generated if not provided.


enable_ha
bool
Whether to enable High Availability (HA) mode with leader election. Defaults to True.





Methods

run()
Starts the scheduler’s main processing loop. This is an async method.
async def run(self) -> None
The scheduler will connect to NATS and, if it becomes the leader (or if HA is disabled), it will start polling for jobs that are ready to be enqueued.



High Availability (HA)
When enable_ha is True, you can run multiple Scheduler instances for redundancy. They will use a leader election protocol built on a NATS KV store to ensure that only one instance is actively scheduling jobs at any given time. If the leader instance goes down, another instance will automatically take over. ## Service Layer Integration
The Scheduler has been enhanced with the new service layer architecture to provide better integration with the ServiceManager and improved reliability.


Using Scheduler with ServiceManager
For applications using the service layer architecture, it’s recommended to use the ServiceManager for scheduler operations:
from naq.services.manager import ServiceManager
from naq.services.base import ServiceConfig
from naq.services.scheduler import SchedulerService

# Create service manager
service_manager = ServiceManager(config=ServiceConfig())
await service_manager.initialize_all()

# Get scheduler service
scheduler_service = service_manager.get_service("scheduler", SchedulerService)

# Add a schedule
from naq.services.scheduler import Schedule
schedule = Schedule(
    id="my_schedule",
    func=my_function,
    cron="0 */5 * * * *",  # Every 5 minutes
    args=(1, 2),
    kwargs={"key": "value"}
)
await scheduler_service.add_schedule(schedule)

# Start the scheduler
await scheduler_service.start()

# Get all schedules
schedules = await scheduler_service.get_all_schedules()
for schedule in schedules:
    print(f"Schedule: {schedule.id}, Cron: {schedule.cron}")

# Stop the scheduler
await scheduler_service.stop()

# Clean up
await service_manager.cleanup_all()


High Availability with Service Layer
The service layer enhances the High Availability (HA) features of the scheduler:
from naq.services.scheduler import SchedulerServiceConfig

# Configure scheduler for high availability
config = SchedulerServiceConfig(
    enable_ha=True,
    leader_election_ttl=30,
    heartbeat_interval=10,
    max_missed_heartbeats=3
)

scheduler_service = SchedulerService(config=config)

# Monitor scheduler status
status = await scheduler_service.get_status()
print(f"Is leader: {status.is_leader}")
print(f"Active schedulers: {status.active_schedulers}")
print(f"Last heartbeat: {status.last_heartbeat}")

title: Development Workflow
text:
This document describes the development workflow and CI/CD pipeline for the naq project.


The naq project uses a comprehensive development workflow that includes automated testing, code quality checks, and documentation generation. The CI/CD pipeline ensures that all changes are thoroughly tested before being merged into the main branch.



The CI/CD pipeline is defined in .github/workflows/test.yml and runs on every push to the main and develop branches, as well as on every pull request.





Checkout: Retrieves the source code
Python Setup: Sets up the required Python version (3.12, 3.13)
Install uv: Installs the uv package manager
Install Dependencies: Installs project dependencies using uv pip install -e .[dev,test]





Linting: Runs ruff check src/ to check for code style and potential issues
Formatting: Runs ruff format --check src/ to verify code formatting
Type Checking: Runs ruff check src/ --select E,F,W for type validation




The pipeline runs tests in stages to provide clear feedback on different types of failures:


pytest tests/test_models/ tests/test_services/ tests/test_config/ tests/test_cli/ -v

Tests individual components in isolation
Includes model, service, configuration, and CLI tests
Fast execution with mocked dependencies




pytest tests/test_integration/ -v

Tests interactions between components
Requires a running NATS server (provided as a service)
Includes end-to-end scenarios and smoke tests




pytest tests/test_compatibility/ -v

Tests API compatibility and user workflows
Ensures backward compatibility
Validates user-facing functionality




pytest tests/test_performance/ -v

Tests performance benchmarks and memory usage
Identifies performance regressions
Monitors resource utilization






The CI pipeline includes a NATS server as a service for integration tests:
services:
  nats:
    image: nats:2.10
    ports:
      - 4222:4222
      - 8222:8222
    options: >-
      --health-cmd "wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:8222/varz || exit 1"
      --health-interval 10s
      --health-timeout 5s
      --health-retries 5



The pipeline installs both development and testing dependencies:
uv pip install -e .[dev,test]
This includes: - pytest: Test framework - pytest-mock: Mocking utilities - pytest-asyncio: Async test support - freezegun: Time-based testing - ruff: Code quality and formatting







Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/legout/naq.git
cd naq
Install dependencies:
uv pip install -e .[dev,test]
Start NATS server (for integration tests):
cd docker
docker-compose up -d






pytest



# Unit tests
pytest tests/test_models/ tests/test_services/ tests/test_config/ tests/test_cli/

# Integration tests
pytest tests/test_integration/

# Compatibility tests
pytest tests/test_compatibility/

# Performance tests
pytest tests/test_performance/



pytest tests/test_services/test_my_service.py



pytest tests/test_services/test_my_service.py::test_my_service_initialization






ruff check src/



ruff format src/



ruff check src/ --select E,F,W




# Format code
ruff format src/

# Check for issues
ruff check src/

# Run type checking
ruff check src/ --select E,F,W

# Run tests
pytest




The test suite is organized into the following directories:

tests/test_models/: Tests for data models and structures
tests/test_services/: Tests for service layer components and utilities
tests/test_integration/: Tests for integration between components
tests/test_compatibility/: Tests for API compatibility and user workflows
tests/test_performance/: Tests for performance benchmarks and memory usage
tests/test_config/: Tests for configuration system components
tests/test_cli/: Tests for command-line interface functionality




When contributing to the project:

Create a feature branch from develop
Write tests for your changes
Run all checks locally before committing
Submit a pull request to the develop branch
Ensure CI/CD pipeline passes

For more detailed contribution guidelines, see Contributing.







If integration tests fail due to NATS connection issues: 1. Ensure NATS server is running: docker-compose ps 2. Check NATS logs: docker-compose logs nats 3. Restart NATS: docker-compose restart nats



If tests fail locally: 1. Ensure all dependencies are installed: uv pip install -e .[dev,test] 2. Check for missing test files: ls tests/ 3. Run tests with verbose output: pytest -v



If code quality checks fail: 1. Run formatting: ruff format src/ 2. Fix linting issues: ruff check --fix src/ 3. Check for type errors: ruff check src/ --select E,F,W





The CI/CD pipeline is designed to run efficiently: - Unit tests run in parallel and complete quickly - Integration tests run only after unit tests pass - Performance tests are isolated to prevent false positives - The entire pipeline completes in under 5 minutes



Planned improvements to the CI/CD pipeline: - Code Coverage: Add coverage reporting and thresholds - Documentation Generation: Automated documentation builds - Security Scanning: Integration with security scanning tools - Performance Benchmarking: Historical performance tracking - Multi-platform Testing: Testing across different operating systems
